topics.name: 3.1.1 Creation
points: Forms of expression: Michelangelo's Creation of Adam and one other artistic depiction of creation
Beliefs: God as creator in Genesis 1 and 2; transcendent and omnipotent
Beliefs: humans made in the image of God: free will, stewardship, human dignity and sanctity of life
Scripture: the Bible's origin, structure and literary forms; inspiration; interpretations of Genesis
Tradition: natural law; Magisterium: Vatican II and science and religion (Gaudium et Spes 36)
Practices: caring for the environment and stewardship; CAFOD's sustainability work

topics.name: 3.1.2 Incarnation
points: Forms of expression: Ichthus, Alpha and Omega, Chi-Rho; religious art and statues of Jesus
Beliefs: Jesus as incarnate Son (Luke 1, Matthew 1) and divine Word (John 1)
Beliefs: Jesus fully human and fully God; Son of Man and Son of God (Mark 8:31, 14:61-62)
Scripture: Jesus as fulfilment of the law and model of virtue; the Beatitudes and Matthew 25:31-46
Tradition: Irenaeus; Magisterium: Dei Verbum 4 and Verbum Domini 12
Practices: grace and the sacramental nature of reality; the seven sacraments
Practices: imago dei and the protection of the unborn (Luke 1:44)

topics.name: 3.1.3 The Triune God, Mission and Prayer
points: Forms of expression: music in worship (psalms, plainchant, hymns, worship songs), Mass settings and Eucharistic acclamations
Beliefs: the Trinity in the Nicene Creed and its scriptural roots
Beliefs: the Trinity and Genesis 1:1-3; mission and evangelism as work of the Spirit
Scripture: Mark 1:9-11 and Galatians 4:6-7; Tradition: Augustine and Catherine LaCugna
Magisterium: councils of Nicaea and Constantinople
Practices: baptism as initiation into the life of the Trinity
Practices: prayer (traditional and spontaneous) and posture in worship

topics.name: 3.1.4 Redemption
points: Forms of expression: church architecture and design; lectern, altar, crucifix and tabernacle
Beliefs: redemption through the death, resurrection and ascension of Jesus
Beliefs: views on salvation and grace; redemption and the liturgy
Scripture: Mark 15, John 20, Acts 1 and 2; Tradition: Irenaeus and Anselm on salvation
Magisterium: conscience (Gaudium et Spes 16)
Practices: the Mass as source and summit; Words of Institution, Agnus Dei, Real Presence, sacrifice of the Mass
Practices: Eucharistic adoration

topics.name: 3.1.5 Church and the Kingdom of God
points: Forms of expression: Stations of the Cross, pilgrimage (Jerusalem, Rome, Walsingham, Lourdes) and drama
Beliefs: the Kingdom of God in the Lord's Prayer; justice, peace and reconciliation
Beliefs: Church hierarchy and Vatican II and its four key documents
Scripture: Mary as model of discipleship and the Magnificat
Tradition: four marks of the Church and apostolic succession; Magisterium: Catholic social teaching
Practices: Catholic agencies working locally and nationally/globally
Practices: vocation and the life of one important Catholic figure

topics.name: 3.1.6 Eschatology
points: Forms of expression: the Paschal candle, Michelangelo's Last Judgement and memorials
Beliefs: resurrection and life after death (1 Corinthians 15:42-44)
Beliefs: the four last things; purgatory; particular and final judgement
Scripture: the Rich Man and Lazarus; Tradition: Julian of Norwich; Magisterium: Lumen Gentium 48
Practices: the last rites and the funeral rite
Practices: sanctity of life, care for the dying and euthanasia

topics.name: Islam
points: Beliefs: the six articles of faith (Sunni) and five roots of Usul ad-Din (Shi'a)
Beliefs: Tawhid (Surah 112) and the nature of God
Beliefs: angels, including Jibril and Mika'il
Beliefs: predestination, human freedom and the Day of Judgement
Beliefs: Akhirah: life after death, resurrection, heaven and hell
Beliefs: Risalah: Adam, Ibrahim and Muhammad
Beliefs: holy books: the Qur'an, Torah, Psalms, Gospel and Scrolls of Abraham
Beliefs: the Imamate in Shi'a Islam
Practices: Five Pillars of Sunni Islam and Ten Obligatory Acts of Shi'a Islam
Practices: Shahadah
Practices: Salah (including Jummah) and differences between Sunni and Shi'a prayer
Practices: Sawm during Ramadan and the Night of Power
Practices: Zakah and Khums
Practices: Hajj
Practices: Jihad: greater and lesser jihad
Practices: festivals in Great Britain: Id-ul-Adha, Id-ul-Fitr and Ashura

topics.name: Judaism
points: Beliefs: the nature of God (One, Creator, Law-Giver and Judge, loving and merciful) and the Shekhinah
Beliefs: the afterlife: judgement and resurrection
Beliefs: the Messiah
Beliefs: the Covenant with Abraham and the Promised Land (Genesis 12:1-3)
Beliefs: the Covenant at Sinai and the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:1-17)
Beliefs: key moral principles (justice, healing the world, charity, kindness) and Pikuach Nefesh
Beliefs: free will and the 613 mitzvot
Practices: the synagogue: importance and design features; Orthodox and Reform synagogues
Practices: public worship, the Amidah and Shabbat
Practices: home worship, private prayer and the Tenakh and Talmud
Practices: rituals: Brit Milah, Bar and Bat Mitzvah, marriage and mourning
Practices: dietary laws (kosher and trefah)
Practices: festivals: Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Pesach

topics.name: Theme A Religion, relationships and families
points: Love and sexuality: Catholic teaching on sexual love; Theology of the Body
Sex before marriage, adultery and same-sex relationships: Christian and non-religious views
Marriage: valid Catholic marriage, vows, annulment, divorce and remarriage
Cohabitation, same-sex marriage and ethical arguments about divorce
Roles in the family; Catholic family planning; purpose of the family
Artificial contraception; same-sex and single parents
Equality of women and men; gender prejudice and discrimination

topics.name: Theme B Religion, peace and conflict
points: Violence, bullying, justice, forgiveness and reconciliation
Righteous anger and violent protest
Just war theory and the effects of war
Nuclear weapons, weapons of mass destruction and nuclear deterrence
Holy war, religion as a cause of war and responses to victims
Pacifism in Catholic and Papal teaching
Terrorism, torture, radicalisation and martyrdom
Peacemaking, conflict resolution organisations and nonviolent resistance

topics.name: Theme C Religion, human rights and social justice
points: Human rights, human dignity and religious freedom
Rights and responsibilities
Wealth: stewardship, wealth creation, exploitation and human trafficking; the Church's wealth
Greed, materialism and sacrificing possessions
Poverty: the preferential option for the poor; CAFOD or Christian Aid
Responsibility for helping those in poverty
Racial prejudice and discrimination; equality and justice
Prejudice in religion (gender, sexuality); positive discrimination and tolerance

topics.name: Theme D St Mark's Gospel: the life of Jesus (textual study)
points: John's preparation (1:1-8) and Jesus' baptism and temptation (1:9-13)
The paralysed man (2:1-12) and Jairus' daughter (5:21-24a, 35-43)
The rejection at Nazareth (6:1-6) and the feeding of the five thousand (6:30-44)
Caesarea Philippi (8:27-33) and the Transfiguration (9:2-9)
Passion prediction (10:32-34) and James and John's request (10:35-45)
Bartimaeus (10:46-52) and the entry into Jerusalem (11:1-11)
The Last Supper (14:12-26) and Gethsemane (14:32-52)
The trials before the Jewish authorities (14:53, 57-65) and Pilate (15:1-15)
The crucifixion and burial (15:21-47) and the empty tomb (16:1-8)
Significance: titles of Jesus for 1st-century Jews and 21st-century Christians
Significance: Jesus as teacher and miracle worker; historicity of miracles
Significance: the Last Supper, death and resurrection; authority of Mark's Gospel

topics.name: Theme E St Mark's Gospel as a source of spiritual truth (textual study)
points: Parables of the sower (4:1-9, 14-20), growing seed (4:26-29) and mustard seed (4:30-32)
Jesus and the children (10:13-16), the rich man (10:17-27) and the greatest commandment (12:28-34)
The man with leprosy (1:40-45) and the call of Levi (2:13-17)
The Syro-Phoenician woman's daughter (7:24-30) and the epileptic boy (9:14-29)
The widow at the treasury (12:41-44) and the anointing at Bethany (14:1-9)
The call of the first disciples (1:16-20) and the woman with a haemorrhage (5:24b-34)
The mission of the Twelve (6:7-13) and the cost and rewards of discipleship (8:34-38; 10:28-31)
Peter's denials (14:27-31, 66-72) and the commission and ascension (16:14-20)
Significance: the Kingdom of God (present, future, inner, communal)
Significance: Jesus' attitudes to those disregarded by society, then and now
Significance: discipleship and faith; authority of Jesus' teaching
